name: TGV
summary: TGV uses stacked germanium detectors and thin isotope foils to investigate double-beta processes, including double-electron capture of cadmium-106. Its TGV-II configuration operated at the Modane underground laboratory.
detection_principle: Cadmium foils are sandwiched between low-background planar HPGe detectors. Coincident characteristic X rays following electron capture provide a signature, while the stack geometry rejects uncorrelated backgrounds.

status.label: Status not established
status.evidence: Published TGV-II work documents low-background double-electron-capture searches with enriched cadmium-106 at Modane. The cited historical literature does not establish the current operating status.

key_parameters.name: Underground shielding
key_parameters.value: Approximately 4800 metres water equivalent at Modane

results.summary: The TGV-II publication reported preliminary limits on double-electron capture and positron/electron-capture channels of 106Cd from a low-background measurement at Modane.

science_scope: A neutrinoless double-beta-decay signal would establish lepton-number violation. Converting a half-life constraint into an effective Majorana mass requires a decay mechanism and nuclear matrix elements; a null search is not a neutrino-mass measurement.
